name: Ship deck
description: The fleet as a ship at sea in hi-bit pixel art: machines are deck sections, lanes are sailors, the lookout crow brings what waits on you on a parchment dialog, and the ship's log below the waterline carries the facts.

fonts.author: The Soft Type Project Authors (Sarah Cadigan-Fried)
fonts.modified: subset (Latin + board punctuation) and converted to WOFF2; no Reserved Font Name

fonts.author: The Atkinson Hyperlegible Next Project Authors (Braille Institute, Applied Design Works, Letters From Sweden)
fonts.modified: subset (Latin + board punctuation) and converted to WOFF2; no Reserved Font Name

grid.tv_rule: ap_dev = max(1, floor(min(viewport_w_dev / 640, viewport_h_dev / 360))); ap_css = ap_dev / devicePixelRatio
grid.phone_rule: ap_dev = max(2, round(2 * devicePixelRatio)); ap_css = ap_dev / devicePixelRatio
grid.pixel_font: fp_dev = ceil(14 * devicePixelRatio / 11); label font-size = 11 * fp_dev / devicePixelRatio CSS px
grid.numeral_font: font-size = 27 * n / devicePixelRatio CSS px for a whole n (device px per font px)
grid.centre: offsets floored to whole device px
grid.smoothing: image-rendering: pixelated on every bitmap; canvases at one canvas px per art px

space.$comment: Every length is a whole number of art px. Steps, then named roles.

type.$comment: Sizes in art px (ap). One pixel-face font px is a whole number of art px, so pixel type lands on the grid. tv_4k/tv_1080 give device px; arcminutes are cap height at 3 m (research c.1). Phone sizes are CSS px at DPR 3; docs/theme-spec.md gives the rule for other DPRs.

label.use: labels, state words, ages, ranges, machine names, log header

label_lg.use: HAILING in place of the countdown digit while a try is in flight

numeral.use: clock, landed score, all-clear count line

numeral_hero.use: the count on the call band (the biggest number on the board)

numeral_countdown.use: seconds to the next hail (host down)

title_log.use: lane titles in the ship's log

statement.use: 'Nothing waits on you.' on the anchor plate; hailing sentence

body.use: where to act, other calls, log details, bar sub-lines: the TV floor

body_quiet.use: the one quiet line on the anchor plate

color.$comment: status and text neutrals (status, ink) come from the default theme and never change per theme. surface fills the core's surface roles; scene is art only.

time_of_day.rule: the sky follows the clock; the plate palette follows quiet hours (night) and the anchor screen (sleep)

scene_module.status: ported from concepts/d-shipdeck/js/art.js; draws the anchor, hailing and dark-section art from this spec
scene_module.missing: the core falls back to the plain ground; nothing is lost because the scene says nothing alone

tv.$comment: Art px on the 640 x 360 canvas. Plates are the only places text sits.

bar.critical: becomes the alarm: CRITICAL word and title replace the voyage chart; trouble frame

holds: top call: glyph, title (2 lines max), where to act, detail (1 line), age
up to 3 more calls: glyph, title (1 line), age
also line when 3 or fewer calls wait
call.overflow: with more than 4 calls the 4th row reads '+N more waiting, on the phone'; the count is always the total

scene.rule: full bleed behind the plates; mood only, nothing is said only by the scene

machines.per: one hull plate per machine section: pip, name, word
machines.overflow: a 5th machine and beyond fold into '+N' on the last plate; the phone lists all

log.overflow: more than 6 off-course lanes: 5 rows, then one overflow row (see components.log)

since.when: the screen comes back after display.since_last.min_away_min: landed, new calls, newly stuck

lists.holds: the door to the page board (#/board), left of the key; it grows leftwards for a longer word; never on the television profile

legend.when: the key is open (over the whole upper area): every glyph shape with its word, what the sea's things mean, when each creature was last seen and the replay of the last event

open.$comment: The open sea: nothing waits on the viewer, so the call plate is one banner line and the scene window is the whole upper area. A call brings the panel and the window above back.

holds: the all-clear in one line: 'Nothing waits on you', then the calm line, cut to fit (said in full to a screen reader)
one pip, name and word per machine

banner.content: the scene cropped to the ship; replaced by the hailing plate when the host is down

call.rule: on a 390 x 844 viewport the call band's top edge is at or above 320 CSS px; every call is shown in full with its detail

log.rule: every off-course lane, one per block, no overflow row

phone.anchor: not used: the phone shows the night board (it is opened on purpose)

motion.$comment: Announce once, then rest (research b.2-13, c.7). Durations in ms; 'steps' = discrete frames, never eased.

levels.full: arrivals, one-shot transitions, idle crew loops on lanes that changed in the last idle.window_s (at most idle.max_sprites); the ambient sea at normal size
levels.calm: arrivals and one-shot transitions; a changed lane's crew sprite plays idle.calm_burst_s then rests; no continuous crew loop; the ambient sea at its smallest amplitude and slowest tempo
levels.still: no animation, no ambient sea; every change is instant

motion.reduced_motion: prefers-reduced-motion or config motion=still: every transition becomes an instant change (or a cross-fade of at most 100 ms); no idle; the hail countdown and the clock still update, as plain digit swaps

never: quiet hours except a new call or critical

bounce.what: the count on the call band

idle.what: crew sprites whose lane changed step or reported in the window; the sea and the ship's float are the separate ambient channel below; smoke, lantern and flags never idle

ambient.what: The sea and the ship's float: a channel apart from the alert motion above. Whole art px, stepped frames, never eased, one canvas px per art px. It never touches a plate or any text. Off under level still, prefers-reduced-motion, config display.ambient false, a hidden tab and a scene scrolled out of view.

calm.what: the TV default: on, at its smallest amplitude and slowest tempo

night.what: night and quiet hours: slow and small

storm.what: a critical: bigger, faster swell, harder roll

anchor.what: moored: a tiny bob, no roll, a slow sea

hail.what: the host does not answer: the swell slows

lost.what: every source lost: the sea and the ship hold still (only the burn-in drift runs)

fog.what: a silent section: the swell slows

lean.what: masthead sway: a whole-px row shear about the waterline

pitch.what: bow and stern rise and fall: a whole-px column shear about the hull's middle

surge.what: slow forward drift of the ship against the sea

heave.what: the swell: wave dashes ride up and down by whole rows

burn_in.what: clouds, the haze and the horizon keep moving even when the swell holds still, so no pixel line stays put for hours

drift.moves: all plates together; the scene canvas stays put (it changes on its own with the sky)
drift.under_reduced_motion: kept: one whole-art-px jump every 4 min is not perceived motion

anchor_drift.path: clockwise round the box edge (48 positions, 3 h 12 min a lap)
anchor_drift.moves: the anchor plate, the ship and the crow together

fill_exceptions: the call plate by day (the one light block)
burn_in.bright_static: no static logo or wordmark; chrome labels in ink2

oled_safe.effect: the day call plate uses the night parchment (dark plate, amber band stays) so no large light block sits on the panel for hours

crt.layer: scene canvas only, never a plate
crt.dark_rows_dev: max(1, floor(ap_dev / 3)) device px at the bottom of each art-px row

uses: fog over the whole sea when lost
the stale half of a range bar

call.title: title
call.detail: body in call_ink2, 1 line on the TV
call.rows: body; glyph in its slot; age as label
call.rule: dashed 1 ap in call_edge between the top call and the rows
call.cursor: 7 x 4 ap continue mark in call_ink, bottom right
call.arrival: crow flies in (crow_flight), plate unrolls (open, 4 steps), band blinks 3 at 2 Hz, count bounces twice; then still

calm.big: numeral 'Nothing waits on you' is words, not a zero
calm.lines: body in ink2: what is under way and landed, in words
calm.crow: rests on the stern rail in the scene

alarm.title: title in ink
alarm.scene: storm weather, 1-art-px trouble edge round the canvas (blinks 3 at 2 Hz on arrival, then steady)
alarm.machine: the machine the critical is on shows the alert pip and ALERT (fix: never OK while critical)

machines.fix: a machine with a critical on it reads ALERT in trouble

log.header: label in ink2: SHIP'S LOG, n OFF COURSE; counts under way / scouting / landed with their glyphs
log.row: glyph | title_log | state word (label, slot from state map) | detail (body, ink2) | range (label) + bar 30 x 4 ap | machine (label, ink2)
log.last_known: a row from a silent source keeps its state word and adds 'LAST KNOWN' (label, fog) beside it; title and range turn fog; the glyph slot is dithered

overflow.shows: rows_max - 1 rows in the one order (theme-spec 24.2), then one row: '+N more: 2 working, 1 stuck. Full list on the Gun deck.'
overflow.style: body in ink2, no glyph, no bar

log.wrap: a detail may wrap once; if the log would still overflow, details truncate with an ellipsis before any row folds

notice.title: notice_title: 'Lost contact, no report for {t}'
notice.body: body: 'Everything below is last known, as of {hh:mm}.'
notice.scene: fog rolls over the whole sea (fog_roll); every deck lantern goes dark; crew turn to dithered ghosts
notice.log: rows keep state words with LAST KNOWN beside them

dark_section.when: one machine's source is silent, or its health beat is lost
dark_section.scene: that deck section goes dark: its mast lantern is swapped to lantern_dark (lamp_out), a fog bank rolls over it (fog_roll), its crew become dithered ghosts in their last pose
dark_section.plate: its hull plate shows the silent pip and 'SILENT 16 MIN' (or 'LOST 16 MIN' for a lost beat) in fog
dark_section.calls: its calls stay in the call plate with 'as of hh:mm' and a frozen age
dark_section.draining: a draining machine keeps its lantern lit, shows the warn pip and DRAINING; no fog

anchor.when: quiet hours AND no call waits AND no critical AND the host answers AND at least one source is live AND TV layout
anchor.wake: any call, critical, host down or loss of every source ends it at once; after the last call resolves at night the board waits settle_s before anchoring

scene.sky: scene.sky.anchor, light scene.light.anchor, static stars (no twinkle), moon placed by the clock
scene.ship: centred (zones.tv.anchor.ship), sails furled (sail.furled), anchor chain from the bow to the waterline, deck lanterns dark
scene.lantern: one lantern_lit on the stern: the only warm light; it never flickers
scene.crew: every sailor in a hammock (landed, idle and working crew alike); off-course crew keep their marks above the hammock (clock, crate, smoke) drawn in fog
scene.crow: crow_asleep on the stern rail, with the asleep glyph above it in fog
scene.weather: kept but dimmed: rain over a struggling section, fog over a silent one; never a storm (a critical wakes the board)

lines.text: one quiet line: what is still off course and any machine not ok, then 'Quiet hours until {t}.' (2 lines max)
trust: lamp pip and 'n/n LIVE, NEWEST 6 S'

anchor.motion: anchor_in (4 steps: plates fade out, sails furl, lanterns go out one by one, the crow settles) under calm or full; instant under still. Then nothing moves except the clock digits and the drift.

hail.replaces: the scene window (TV) or the banner (phone); the bar, call and log stay as last known
hail.when: the page has had no answer from its host for thresholds.host_down_after_s

scene.masthead: the masthead lantern goes dark (lamp_out); a two-flag hoist (flag_halves over flag_checks) runs up the mainmast halyard (flag_hoist, once)
scene.sky: thin fog over the sky (fog_roll); sea and ship otherwise frozen
scene.crew: frozen in their last pose; no idle
scene.bell: the ship's bell (bell sprite) on the hailing plate strikes once per retry (bell_strike: a 1-sprite-px swing, 2 frames); drawn at 3 ap per sprite px

plate.frame: ink2 1 ap, panel_lo 1 ap, ink2 1 ap (a double rope line, not a status hue)

tv_lines.text: the bell (sprite at 3 ap per sprite px, 36 x 36 ap) beside the seconds to the next try

tv_bar.title: This board can't reach its host. (title, ink)
tv_bar.sub: Newest data from 19:29, 51 s ago. (body, ink2)

phone_lines.text: bell beside the seconds to the next try
This board can't reach its host.
LIKELY | the host is asleep or restarting, the process stopped, or this device lost the network

countdown.tick: every second, an instant digit swap (allowed at every motion level)
countdown.at_zero: the digit is replaced by 'HAILING' (label_lg, 7 x 14 = 98 ap wide) for the request; on failure the bell strikes once and the count restarts; on success the plate closes (resolve) and the lantern relights

hail.night: night palette; the bell strike and flag hoist still play once (they are the news), the lantern stays dark
hail.phone: the plate replaces the banner, full width; countdown at numeral_countdown phone size

empty.scene: the ship at anchor by day with bare masts
empty.plate: notice_title 'No machine has reported yet' + body how to send a feed

loading.plate: label 'READING THE LOG' + dashed placeholder lines

words.$comment: Theme vocabulary layered under config labels (config wins). Plain words; the nautical ones are names, never the only explanation.
words.deck_gun_deck_what: every lane, grouped by goal, else by project
words.deck_chart_room_what: what is queued next, and what it waits for
words.deck_logbook_what: what this screen showed, and the key
words.item_gone_body: Gone from the board since {t}: answered, landed or dropped.
words.all_clear_last: Nothing waited at the last report
words.log_more: +{n} more: {by_state}. Full list on the Gun deck.
words.lost_body: Everything below is last known, as of {t}.
words.hail_title: This board can't reach its host.
words.calm_line: {moving} under way, {off} off course, {waiting} waiting, {landed} landed {when}.

checks.method: WCAG 2 contrast ratio; CVD = OKLab distance x 100 after Machado 2009 simulation at severity 1 (research c.4)
